questions: Should the x-axis indices be 0-based integer indices regardless of the original data's indexing (e.g., if the JSON list is nested under a key that implies a different index mapping)?
If the extracted data is not a list but a single numeric value, should it be treated as a Series of length 1, and if so, how should normalization and plotting behave?
Does the function need to handle non-numeric data within the extracted list (e.g., strings that can be converted to floats, or mixed types), and if so, should it raise an error or attempt conversion?
Should the plot's x-axis ticks be explicitly set to match the indices (e.g., integer ticks from 0 to n-1), or left to matplotlib's default tick generation?
Is the MinMaxScaler expected to be fitted on the entire values array, or should normalization be applied per some other scope (e.g., per batch if data is streamed)?
If the data contains NaN or infinite values, should they be handled, ignored, or cause an error during normalization?
Should the returned pd.Series have an explicit index (e.g., RangeIndex starting at 0) or preserve any index from the original data (though JSON lists have no inherent index)?
Are there any constraints on the plot size, figure DPI, or should the function save the plot to a file, or only return the Axes object?
